extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, spokespeople, startup founders and anyone pitching journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating press/ media pitches that attract journalists and earn coverage; focuses on topic selection, presentation, and tailoring to reporters. Short practical how-to advice for PR practitioners and communicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have an interesting topic.
rubrics_metrics.description: If your pitch isn’t interesting, attention-grabbing or tailored to the journalist, it won’t get coverage. Many routine announcements (product launch, funding round, product update) are simply not that interesting no matter how you spin them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the core news is uninteresting, try to tie it to something journalists and bloggers haven’t heard before. Example: if you hire a high-profile data scientist, craft a story around the data he uncovered and 'sneak in the tidbit' about his move to your company. If you have a relationship with a journalist or reach out at the right time you may place the announcement, but usually you need a stronger story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grab attention.
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you’ve come up with an interesting topic, present it in an interesting way so recipients will actually read the pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid long paragraphs of text — no one likes to read them, and if no one reads your pitch, no one will write about it. Make the presentation concise and attention-grabbing (the article is paywalled before listing further tactics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor the pitch to the journalist.
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitches that are not tailored to the journalist are unlikely to get coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied advice: customize angle and relevance for the specific journalist or outlet rather than sending generic, one-size-fits-all releases; leverage existing relationships and timing when possible.
